title: Lightweight scheduling probe for prefill/decode per-kernel metrics
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: add a low-overhead profiling probe that ties scheduler decisions (slice assignment, latency budget, attention kernel variant) to per-kernel execution metrics for prefill and decode paths. This probe should enable us to answer: (1) why the scheduler chose a specific kernel variant for a slice, (2) which attention optimization (e.g., fused attention, rotary/ALiBi variants) contributed to kernel latency differences, and (3) how prefill/decode scheduling heuristics correlate with kernel-level hotpaths at 99th percentile without adding >2% wall-clock overhead.

Scope: implement an inline, probabilistic sampling layer in the runtime scheduler that annotates trace spans and NVTX ranges with a small set of standardized tags (slice_id hash, kernel_selector_tag, attention_mode, prefill_or_decode, seq_len_bucket). Emit compact per-kernel counters and micro-latencies (enqueue, kernel_start, kernel_end) into our existing metrics pipeline (Prometheus pushgateway -> metrics pipeline) and trace system (Jaeger/Grafana Tempo). Provide a Grafana dashboard and a short Runbook for interpreting kernel attribution signals.

Non-goals: full payload-level KV cache fingerprinting, heavy-weight continuous tracing for every request, or changes to current kernel selection heuristics as part of this ticket. Those will be follow-ups once telemetry validates hypotheses.
acceptance_criteria: Probe compiles behind a runtime feature flag and can be toggled at runtime without restart
End-to-end pipeline: sampled events show up in traces with the standardized tags and in Prometheus with per-kernel counters within 30s
Measured overhead (p50 latency increase) <= 2% and memory/_temp allocations <= 5MB per worker when probe is enabled at 1% sampling
Grafana dashboard has panels for per-kernel 50/95/99 latencies, kernel selection distribution by seq_len_bucket, and scheduler decision heatmap
Documentation: runtime/telemetry page and short runbook added with examples and troubleshooting steps
One cross-team demo with PM/Observability/Inference SRE and sign-off recorded in comments
steps: Design: finalize tag schema (kernel_selector_tag, attention_mode, slice_hash, seq_len_bucket, path=pre/decode)
Implement lightweight sampler in scheduler that emits a compact event object and annotates NVTX ranges and trace spans
Add minimal per-kernel counters: enqueue_count, start_count, complete_count, enqueue_latency_ms, execution_latency_ms
Wire metrics to current metrics exporter (add labels: model, model_version, variant, region, kernel_selector_tag)
Create Grafana dashboard template and runbook draft
Internal rollout: enable 0.1% sampling in staging, validate overhead and signal quality; then 1% in canary; then 5% in limited production for short window
Post-rollout: capture findings, create follow-up tickets for scheduler heuristic changes or heavier sampling if useful
risks: Excessive cardinality from free-form kernel tags; mitigate with a strict enumerated kernel_selector_tag registry
Edge-case overhead for very short-lived slices (sub-ms): ensure sampler bypass for seq_len_bucket < 8
Metrics explosion if sampling rate is increased without aggregation/rollup; add rate-limits and downsampling in exporter
Privacy/compliance: ensure no request-level PII is emitted (use stable hashed slice IDs only)
